name: lout
desc: Text formatting like TeX, but simpler
why: A TeX-like typesetting language with its own markup grammar, an obscure old-school alternative worth an afternoon of playing.

brief.what_it_is: Lout is a document formatting system written by Jeffrey Kingston at the Basser Department of Computer Science, University of Sydney. It reads a high-level plain-text description of a document, similar in style to LaTeX, and produces a PostScript file for printing on most laser printers or graphic display devices. A plain-text output option is also available, along with a PDF mode the project calls highly experimental. The Lout language that drives most typesetting and layout is purely functional. The project lists 16 supported languages for its built-in multilingual support.
brief.why_it_exists: The Savannah summary presents Lout as a LaTeX-like document formatter, with the Lout language implementing most typesetting and layout tasks. It also stresses that the system is inherently multilingual and that adding new languages is easy. The README and docs were not reached, so no further author framing is available.
brief.how_it_works: The source document is a high-level description that Lout processes into PostScript output, with plain-text output as an option. The Lout language, in which most layout is implemented, is purely functional. The project's own advice is to generate PostScript and convert it to PDF with GhostScript rather than use the experimental built-in PDF mode.

brief.standout: Lout is a LaTeX-style formatter built on a purely functional language, and it treats multilingual support as a core design feature rather than an add-on. It is an obscure old-school alternative to TeX, and its maintainer is a University of Sydney computer scientist.
brief.status: Savannah lists Development Status 6 - Mature and a registration date of 19 Aug 2010. The group has 2 members, 2 admins, and 1 public mailing list. No last-release or last-commit date was visible on the summary page, so recent activity is unknown.
brief.caveats: The built-in PDF output is described as highly experimental, and the project suggests using PostScript plus GhostScript instead. The project is not part of the GNU Project even though it is hosted on Savannah. The license is GPL v3 or later. Lout is inherently multilingual. Adding new languages is easy.
The Lout language, in which most document typesetting and layout tasks are implemented, is a purely functional language, which simplifies reasoning about the operations performed.
